subject: Chemistry
title: Chirality and Optical Activity: Mirror Images
summary: A chiral object cannot be superimposed on its mirror image. Chiral molecules rotate plane polarised light: they are optically active. In this lesson: why a left glove does not fit the right hand, plane polarised light from a Nicol prism, the polarimeter, d (+) and l (-), the chiral carbon (four different groups) in butan-2-ol, the 3D mirror test, enantiomers, achiral propan-2-ol, the racemic mixture, and two solved questions.

notes.title: Chirality and Optical Activity
notes.blurb: plane polarised light and optical activity, chirality, enantiomers and the racemic mixture, solved questions

keyPoints: **Chiral**: Like a **left and a right hand**. Achiral: the mirror image **fits**.
**Optical activity**: Light from a **Nicol prism**, angle in a polarimeter. d = **dextrorotatory**, l = **laevorotatory**.
**Chiral carbon**: Stereocentre **C*** in butan-2-ol. Propan-2-ol (two CH₃): **achiral**.

sections.h: Plane polarised light and optical activity

blocks.p: Ordinary light vibrates in every plane. A **Nicol prism** passes only the vibrations of one plane: **plane polarised light**. Some compounds rotate this plane when it passes through their solution: they are **optically active**. The angle is measured in a **polarimeter**.

list: **Chiral** (Greek cheir, hand): an object or molecule whose mirror image cannot be superimposed on it, like a left and a right hand.
**Chiral carbon (stereocentre, C*):** a carbon bonded to four different groups. Butan-2-ol: CH₃–C*H(OH)–C₂H₅ (H, OH, CH₃, C₂H₅).
**Achiral:** the mirror image superimposes. Propan-2-ol has two identical CH₃ groups on C2: achiral, optically inactive.

blocks.p: **The mirror test:** draw butan-2-ol with wedge (towards you) and dash (away) bonds, reflect it, and turn the image round: H and OH match, but CH₃ and C₂H₅ end up on the wrong sides (front ↔ back). It never superimposes.

**Enantiomers** are non-superimposable mirror images. They have identical physical properties (boiling point, density, solubility, refractive index) and rotate plane polarised light by the **same angle in opposite directions**: (+)-butan-2-ol +13.5°, (−)-butan-2-ol −13.5°.
A **racemic mixture** (±, dl) has equal amounts of the two enantiomers: their rotations cancel, so it is optically inactive. Converting one enantiomer into a racemic mixture is **racemisation**.

list: ✗ Every molecule with a carbon is chiral (it needs a carbon with four different groups, or another source of asymmetry).
✗ Enantiomers have different boiling points (they are identical, except in the direction of rotation).
✗ A racemic mixture contains no chiral molecules (it contains both enantiomers in equal amounts).

blocks.p: **Q1.** 2-chlorobutane, CH₃–C*H(Cl)–CH₂CH₃: C2 carries H, Cl, CH₃ and C₂H₅, all different, so it is chiral and has two enantiomers.
**Q2.** A sample of chiral molecules showing zero rotation contains d and l forms in equal amounts: a racemic mixture.

simulation.reason: The idea is a fixed sequence of steps drawn in the video and the notes; there is no continuous variable for a student to explore.

pyq.q: 2-chlorobutane + Cl₂ → C₄H₈Cl₂ (isomers). The total number of optically active isomers shown by C₄H₈Cl₂ obtained in this reaction is ________. (numerical)
pyq.explain: . Cl₂ can replace an H on C1, C2, C3 or C4 of CH₃–CHCl–CH₂–CH₃: 1,2-dichlorobutane (C2 chiral: 2 enantiomers), 2,2- (achiral), 2,3- (two C*: (R,R) and (S,S) active, meso inactive: 2) and, from C4, 1,3-dichlorobutane (C3 chiral: 2). Total 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
